mismatch.message: Replay error: hit is not a function

summary: The wand-of-striking hit path in zap.c:bhitm is wired, but js/zap.js:bhitm stores gb.bhitpos in a local named hit and then calls that coordinate as if it were zap.c:hit(). Rename the coordinate binding so the existing hit-message function runs; re-evaluate the later resist and kill path independently.

source.branch: bhitm WAN_STRIKING / SPE_FORCE_BOLT when magical resistance fails and the attack roll hits a monster
callers: cmd.c z command -> zap.c dozap -> weffects -> bhit -> bhitm
js/cmd.js runZapCommand -> js/zap.js dozap -> weffects -> bhit -> bhitm
dependencies: zap.c resist() is the next called function after hit() and may expose further unported behavior once the collision is fixed

evidence: The independently recorded v5/healer-wand-striking-grid-bug case reaches zap.c:bhitm through an immediate WAN_STRIKING ray and has 48 boundaries; the baseline evaluation at d273b893 reports 0/48 screens and Replay error: hit is not a function.
A direct JS run of this case throws TypeError at js/zap.js:2986 in bhitm; stack continues through bhit (3391), weffects (5308), and dozap (1197).
C zap.c:160-214 assigns gn.notonhead from gb.bhitpos and, in the successful WAN_STRIKING/SPE_FORCE_BOLT attack arm, calls hit(zap_type_text, mtmp, exclam(dmg)) before resist().

JS zap.js:2948 declares const hit = state.gb?.bhitpos (a coordinate), then zap.js:2986 awaits hit(...) in the same arm, shadowing the hit() function defined at zap.js:1680. The coordinate is also read for cansee and map_invisible later; rename that binding at all its uses without changing source order or random draws.
